claims.text: Ultrathin coherent interfaces in HEA multilayer coatings impede dislocation motion.
Ultrathin coherent interfaces in HEA multilayer coatings impede grain-boundary sliding.
Interface-mediated obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding retards creep relative to monolithic HEA coatings.
Magnetron sputtering can produce the proposed nanometer-scale HEA multilayers with coherent interfaces.
Multilayer and monolithic coatings can be prepared with identical overall composition so that engineered interfaces are the controlled difference.
Elevated-temperature static and dynamic loading can be used to investigate time-dependent plastic deformation in HEAs.
Coherent layer interfaces obstruct grain-boundary diffusion.
Dislocation-mediated deformation can govern HEA indentation creep.
Reducing dislocation mobility and grain-boundary sliding reduces the accumulation and mobility of defects responsible for creep.
The multilayer-interface barrier effect increases the activation energy for creep relative to a homogeneous microstructure.
Under identical high-temperature loading, multilayer HEA coatings will have lower creep displacement rates than monolithic HEA coatings.
Under identical high-temperature loading, multilayer HEA coatings will have higher creep activation energies than monolithic HEA coatings.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the multilayer interfacial structure remains stable.
Significant interlayer diffusion or phase transformation will undermine the proposed interface-controlled mechanism.
Nanometer-scale layer thickness is required for effective dislocation blocking.
Dislocation pile-ups or related interface-mediated features should be observable after deformation if the proposed barrier mechanism operates.
